positive_evidence: The exact 4,833-byte receipt and its 30-row closure are internally self-consistent. Every frozen row matched its identity and was non-writable; the receipt itself was mode 0444.
The formation validator is independent of the caller working directory and passed from both the repository and /tmp with no candidate or holdout artifacts present.

The runtime replay structurally matches 139 rows for @mkbabb/parse-that 1.0.0, tsx 4.20.3, esbuild 0.25.12, @esbuild/darwin-arm64 0.25.12, get-tsconfig 4.14.0, and resolve-pkg-maps 1.0.0, along with the package lock, Node binary, and eleven named peer-source identities.

The peer worker imports and calls the actual live parseCssScalar, historical parse-that number parser, and C14 numberValue parser before normalization. The harness retains separate lane exclusions and derives a seven-case intersection from thirteen cases.

The public suite exercises six number-start arms, inherited success and failure prefixes, eight binary64/offset additions, seven predecessor profiles, ordinary and preseeded-ahead diagnostics, six parent-composition cases, twelve no-throw extras, and four geometric work constructions at four UTF-16 sizes.
All three deliberate negative controls were rejected, all four frozen feasibility probes passed, and the subprocess hang control was killed after 50 ms.

The planned H, B, S, and D implementations are mechanically distinct: whole-prefix regex/map; factorized all/any with save/restore; staged then/opt with save/restore; and first-character dispatch with atomic arms. Their frozen probes establish API feasibility under the pinned runtime.
The formation carries zero feature credit and does not falsely claim that current hashes establish actor identity.

findings.finding: The public cases do not cover an explicit sign followed by an integer mantissa and exponent, such as +1e2 or -1e2. They cover unsigned 1e3 and explicit-plus exponents only when the mantissa has a fraction (+12.50E-2 and +.75e+2). All four work constructions are unsigned. A branch-factorized parser can therefore omit exponent handling for signed integer mantissas while satisfying every enumerated public observation and work construction.

required_repairs: Separate pre-author boundary acceptance from the post-four-candidate semantic holdout, and encode one satisfiable phase order in the feature row, lifecycle schema, and validator.

Require distinct immutable review identities and externally authenticated actor/model/task receipts; do not permit content-authored receipt strings or one review identity to satisfy two challenge seats.

Give each author a complete seat-specific initial assignment containing only that seat's exact input identities, and make its executable harness closure exclude all peer prompts, packets, probes, roots, and future payloads.

Add a post-admission candidate-close phase that binds regular non-symlink seat-root files, full transitive import/runtime identities, export identity, and exact immutable candidate hashes before holdout generation.
Add branch cross-product public cases including signed integer exponents and negative signed variants, and route every inherited control profile into executable checks.
Sanitize or bind loader-affecting environment state for validator, public, and peer child processes.
rationale: The exact immutable formation rows, pinned runtime, executable peer doors, public transaction/composition/work checks, negative controls, and four distinct feasibility styles are substantial positive evidence. They do not form a consistent admission boundary: holdout order is impossible, reviewer/task identities are self-asserted, author input isolation is internally unsatisfiable, candidate/import closure is absent, and a basic signed-exponent grammar branch is not killed. Any one of the first five defects is sufficient to reject formation before authors.
